tweets.text:
every problem is a nested solution to a higher level problem ... which makes the product/solution dichotomy not as helpful for product development

it can be helpful to put words to the in-between

Does your org

* Work Big
* Work Small
* Define Big, Work Small
or
* Think Big, Work Small

I'm an unabashed (biased) fan of #4 obviously...

50% of product management

saying the same things over and over again with slight modifications and tweaks until the message has landed ... only to worry that this wasn't the right message in the first place.

I really like this style of one year roadmap ...

keeping options open. progressive refinement. commit at the last responsible moment

outcome oriented 1 pagers.

the key is agreeing as a team on the resolution for 1 pagers (e.g. 1-3 months).

checking my sanity ...

anyone else still social distancing, wearing a mask, not traveling, mostly ordering stuff to be delivered, and (reluctantly) spending their whole risk budget on daycare for their kid(s) so they can still work?
most companies need some type of systems thinking / service design / holistic perspective that spans departments ... and most companies are not designed to empower those roles.
